thread.title: UCLA swimming and diving finishes 20th at NCAA Championships with five All-Americans
thread.title_full: UCLA swimming and diving finishes 20th at NCAA Championships with five All-Americans

author: J. D. Beck
title: UCLA swimming and diving finishes 20th at NCAA Championships with five All-Americans
text:
The University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) swimming and diving team finished 20th overall at the NCAA Championships, achieving its highest placement since the 2018-19 season, according to a March 21 announcement. The Bruins had five athletes receive All-American honors during the four-day event.
This year marked UCLA’s second season as a member of the Big Ten Conference. The team’s performance at the championships was also its best under head coach Jordan Cordry.
Seniors Rosie Murphy and Eden Cheng were among those who earned All-American recognition. Additionally, the Bruins’ 200 medley relay squad received All-American honors for their performance on the opening night. The relay team—composed of Sarah Bennetts, Jada Duncan, Anna Wetteland, and Claudia Yovanovich—finished in 15th place overall, marking UCLA’s first All-American finish in that event since 2015.
Murphy led the team on Thursday by earning her first NCAA All-American honors in the 400 individual medley (IM), setting a new school record with a time of 4:02.22 in preliminaries and finishing seventh in finals with a time of 4:03.55. On Saturday, Murphy added an honorable mention finish in the 200 backstroke with another school record time of 1:51.40 for a twelfth-place result. She also secured her second overall All-American honor of the meet in the 200 IM by qualifying seventh in prelims and finishing eighth in finals with a time of 1:54.18.
Cheng competed at her fourth consecutive NCAA Championships and earned her fourth straight All-American honorable mention on platform diving by placing tenth overall with a score of 291.40.
The results highlight significant progress for UCLA’s swimming and diving program as it continues to compete at a high level within its conference.
